properties.name: A project can remove its kit, and update never brings a removed kit back
properties.rationale: From the root cause fact:root-cause-update-brings-a-hand-removed-kit-back-from-its-receipt-2026-10-19: the receipt's presence was the whole test of "a kit is installed here", a missing kit file is by design read as "give me the kit's copy", there was no recorded state for "removed" and no per-project remove — so `update` wrote ~72 files back into 11 hand-cleaned repos and re-armed itself by rewriting the receipt. Anthony chose "Remove command + guard" (the requirement, accepted 2026-10-19). The cause is corrected, not contained: the receipt now records the removal, and `update` reads the receipt AND whether anything it lists is still there, so the install event is no longer read as a live fact about the project (the same class as fact:defect-a-stale-kit-receipt-silently-decides-whether-the-loop-nudge-is-owed). The single-file case is kept on purpose; it is how a person accepts the kit's copy. The harness refusal closes measurement (3) of the root cause: step 4 of resolve_harnesses (install everything when nobody can be asked) stays for a first install only. Tests first: 8 of 9 cases in tools/test_init.py AKitRemovedStaysRemoved failed on main 5d75151, the field case among them (update exited 0 and wrote 79 paths). Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019Xbw6PG9mXJiU2Sb421fnq
properties.subject: system
properties.summary: `reflow2 init --remove` (preview with --check) takes reflow2's kit out of one project: it deletes the kit files nobody edited and names the edited ones it keeps, strips what the kit appended to .gitignore, .gitattributes, .reflow2.toml and the instruction files, marks .reflow2/kit-version.json removed, and leaves the design store alone. `reflow2 update` now refuses, in its no-kit words, when the receipt says removed or when none of the files it records is left (one deleted file still updates), and a live receipt with no `harnesses` makes a non-interactive update refuse and name `--harness` instead of installing every MCP harness. The wrapper passes `init --remove` through unchanged; SETUP.md documents it.
